A stand-in for cl

Where this file is, and what its paths mean (lane F, 2026-11-05). Restored after the restructure of 2026-11-03 left it out of the tree, as it stood on 2026.10.27, and kept as written. The folder above this one is now build/cmake/config/djinterp/tools/vparse; the window's build, which it calls build/ui/vparse (../../../../ui/vparse from there), is build/cmake/config/ui/vparse (../../../ui/vparse); and the tool's README is docs/djinterp/tools/vparse/README.html.

For a machine with no MSVC: Linux, WSL, CI. It is not part of the build, and nothing in the build refers to it.

cl here is a script that takes cl's command line and compiles with a MinGW-w64 Clang for 64-bit Windows. In front of every unit it puts the standard library, read under the real compiler's identity, and then identity.h, which takes that identity away and puts cl 19.51's in its place — _MSC_VER, _MSC_FULL_VER, _MSVC_LANG and the rest defined, __clang__ and __GNUC__ gone.

Two things follow.

  • CMake identifies the compiler as MSVC 19.51, and takes every branch of every list file that it takes for cl: the flags, the levels cl can and cannot select, uxoxo's own build, the suites' counts.
  • djinterp's env takes the branches it takes under cl, in every unit, and what those branches select is compiled, linked against the MinGW-w64 runtime, and run under Wine.

Running it

It needs clang with lld, a MinGW-w64 GCC for 64-bit Windows (for its headers and libraries: x86_64-w64-mingw32-g++), Ninja and Wine. From the folder above this one, build/cmake/djinterp/tools/vparse in djinterp's tree, vparse and its command line:

chmod +x cl_standin/cl cl_standin/link cl_standin/rc  # an archive drops the bits

export CL_STANDIN_LOG=$PWD/out/standin.units           # optional

cmake -S . -B out/standin -G Ninja \
      -DCMAKE_TOOLCHAIN_FILE=cl_standin/toolchain.cmake \
      -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Release
cmake --build out/standin
ctest --test-dir out/standin

and the window, from its own build, build/ui/vparse, which builds vparse with it:

export CL_STANDIN_REAL_ROOTS=/path/to/uxoxo/inc/imgui  # Dear ImGui keeps its own

cmake -S ../../../../ui/vparse -B out/standin-ui -G Ninja \
      -DCMAKE_TOOLCHAIN_FILE=$PWD/cl_standin/toolchain.cmake \
      -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Release \
      -DUXOXO_ROOT=/path/to/uxoxo
cmake --build out/standin-ui
ctest --test-dir out/standin-ui

Configure should begin The C compiler identification is MSVC 19.51.36260.0 and, in the window's build, report the window as Win32 + Direct3D 11. The tests are the ones cl gets. vparse's build has 21: the tool's three (the model's suite, the command line's, and vparse run over the example grammar), djinterp's foundation suites at C++14, 17, 20 and 23 and its C suites at C99, C11 and C17, vparse's at C++14 to 23, and the argument parser's seven - its C suites at C99, C11 and C17, and its C++ suites at C++98, 14, 17 and 20; its allocation sweep is left out, as under cl, whose linker has no --wrap. The window's has those and its own five, 26: the window's suite, its Dear ImGui suite, and three runs of vparse gui - its help, its version, and a grammar it cannot read -- which find the module, vparse-gui-win64.dll, and load it. cl has no C++11 to select, so the leaves leave that level out.

The argument parser's C++ suites do not pass here (2026.10.27), and they are not the tool's: they stop on their first instructions, at every level, with a read of a low address that Wine reports as a page fault. Its C suites pass in C.UTF-8. The window's build with djinterp's suites left out (-DVPARSE_BUILD_DJINTERP_TESTS=OFF) has the tool's eight, which pass.

Ninja Multi-Config, which the msvc preset uses, works the same way with --config and -C.

The first program Wine runs creates its prefix (~/.wine). Tests started together on a machine with none race to create it, and some fail; run wineboot -i first, or run the tests once with -j1.

CL_STANDIN_REAL_ROOTS names directories, colon-separated, whose sources keep the real identity. Dear ImGui's must: they include <windows.h>, which the MinGW-w64 headers will not read as cl's, and they include none of djinterp, so nothing is lost. CL_STANDIN_LOG names a file that gets a line for each unit: its language, its level, whether it was given /Zc:preprocessor, and whether it kept the real identity. Every unit but Dear ImGui's, CMake's own checks, and the kit's should say traditional=0 real=0: the kit's module, DjinterpCli.cmake, builds djinterp::cli and filesys under it with /utf-8 alone, and its units say traditional=1 real=0.

The toolchain confines what a list file finds to the MinGW-w64 sysroot, as a cross toolchain does: uxoxo's build looks for GLFW, and the machine's own GLFW is nothing a Windows unit can read.

What a run shows, and what it cannot

It shows that the build is right for cl — that CMake, told it has cl, configures what the tool's README (docs/djinterp/tools/vparse/README.html) says it does — and that the code cl is handed, along the branches env takes for it, compiles and runs and passes.

It cannot show that cl accepts that code. The parser is Clang's, which is stricter than cl in places and laxer in others; the warnings are Clang's, not /W4's; and the library is libstdc++ over the MinGW-w64 runtime, not Microsoft's. That runtime is msvcrt.dll, where cl's is the Universal CRT, so a unit that takes cl's branches may call a function msvcrt.dll lacks: ucrt.c supplies each one met so far, to the Universal CRT's contract -- _dupenv_s, which djinterp's argument parser reads the environment with. A flag that tells cl how to read, check or emit is taken for what it means to Clang or dropped. The first build with cl itself is still the one that proves those.

One difference matters to the warnings in particular. CMake hands cl a system include directory as /external:I, and cl judges a header external by where it is; Clang judges one by how it was found. The workbench's model headers sit in djinterp's inc/, which this build passes as a system directory, and are included by relative path: under the stand-in they are the workbench's own and are held to its warnings, under cl itself they are read at /external:W0. GCC and Clang builds check them.

The files

file what
cl the driver: cl's command line in, a MinGW-w64 Clang compile out. A flag it does not know stops it. It holds the lists of standard headers read before the swap; a header a unit includes and its list does not must be added, since the library does not compile as cl's
link links through lld against the MinGW-w64 runtime, statically, with ucrt.c compiled in; a system library named foo.lib becomes -lfoo
ucrt.c what the Universal CRT has and msvcrt.dll does not, under the Universal CRT's names: _dupenv_s
rc stands in for the resource compiler and the manifest tool, which CMake looks for and this build has no work for
identity.h the change of identity
toolchain.cmake puts the three scripts where cl, link and rc would be, confines what is found to the MinGW-w64 sysroot, has CMake's checks link through link as cl's do, and tells ctest to run tests through Wine
override.cmake the link and archive rules, in place of the ones CMake has for link.exe and lib.exe
